epithet.ko: 14개조와 국제연맹을 내걸었으나 상원 비준을 얻지 못한 미국 대통령
epithet.en: US president whose Fourteen Points and League of Nations failed to win the Senate’s ratification

bio.ko: 버지니아에서 태어나 프린스턴 대학교 총장과 뉴저지 주지사를 거쳐 1912년 대통령이 되었고, 취임 첫해 연방 관료 조직에 인종 분리를 들여왔다. 1917년 4월 독일의 무제한 잠수함전을 이유로 참전을 요청했고, 1918년 1월 14개조로 국제연맹과 민족자결의 구상을 내놓았다. 파리 강화회의에서 연맹 규약 기초를 이끌었지만 연맹을 위해 독일에 대한 여러 요구를 양보했다. 1919년 10월 뇌졸중으로 쓰러졌고 타협을 거부해 상원의 조약 비준이 무산되었다. 같은 시기 파머 습격의 「적색 공포」가 벌어졌다. 1919년 노벨 평화상을 받았고 1924년 죽었다.
bio.en: Born in Virginia, he was president of Princeton University and governor of New Jersey before winning the presidency in 1912, and in his first year imposed racial segregation across the federal bureaucracy. In April 1917 he asked Congress to declare war over unrestricted submarine warfare, and in January 1918 set out the Fourteen Points, with a League of Nations and self-determination. At the Paris Peace Conference he presided over the drafting of the League Covenant but conceded much to the other powers to get it. A stroke in October 1919 incapacitated him, and his refusal of a compromise sank the Senate’s ratification of the treaty. The Palmer Raids of the Red Scare came in the same years. He received the 1919 Nobel Peace Prize and died in 1924.

evidence.excerpt: Thomas Woodrow Wilson (December 28, 1856 – February 3, 1924) was the 28th president of the United States
was the 28th president of the United States, serving from 1913 to 1921

evidence.claim: born in Virginia, grew up in the American South
evidence.excerpt: Born in Staunton, Virginia, Wilson grew up in the Southern United States during the American Civil War and Reconstruction era.

evidence.claim: PhD at Johns Hopkins; president of Princeton
evidence.excerpt: After earning a PhD in history and political science from Johns Hopkins University, Wilson taught at several colleges prior to being appointed president of Princeton University
Wilson served as the governor of New Jersey from 1911 to 1913
During his first year as president, Wilson authorized the widespread imposition of racial segregation inside the federal bureaucracy

evidence.claim: asked for war in April 1917 over submarine warfare
evidence.excerpt: In April 1917, Wilson asked Congress for a declaration of war against Germany in response to its policy of unrestricted submarine warfare that sank American merchant ships.
On January 8, 1918, Wilson delivered a speech, known as the Fourteen Points, wherein he articulated his administration's long term war objectives.
Other points included the evacuation of occupied territory, the establishment of an independent Poland, and self-determination for the peoples of Austria-Hungary and the Ottoman Empire.
Wilson himself presided over the committee that drafted the Covenant of the League of Nations.

However, in pursuit of his League of Nations, Wilson conceded several points to the other powers present at the conference. Germany was required to permanently cede territory, pay war reparations, relinquish all of her overseas colonies and dependencies and submit to military occupation in the Rhineland.
On October 2, 1919, Wilson suffered a serious stroke, leaving him paralyzed on his left side

evidence.claim: forced the Nay vote of 19 March 1920
evidence.excerpt: Wilson forced his supporters to vote Nay on March 19, 1920, thereby closing the issue.

Attorney General Palmer from November 1919 to January 1920 launched the Palmer Raids to suppress radical organizations. Over 10,000 people were arrested and 556 aliens were deported, including Emma Goldman.
For his efforts towards creating a lasting world peace, Wilson was awarded the 1919 Nobel Peace Prize.
He died on February 3, 1924, at the age of 67.
was the 28th president of the United States, serving from 1913 to 1921

evidence.claim: attended the Paris Peace Conference and advocated the League of Nations
evidence.excerpt: After the Allied victory in November 1918, Wilson attended the Paris Peace Conference. Wilson successfully advocated for the establishment of a multinational organization, the League of Nations
Wilson served as the governor of New Jersey from 1911 to 1913

epithet.ko: 대전 후반 영국을 이끌고 강화회의에서 독일에 대한 온건론을 편 자유당 총리
epithet.en: Liberal prime minister who led Britain in the later war and argued for moderation towards Germany at the peace conference

bio.ko: 맨체스터의 웨일스인 집안에서 태어나 급진 자유주의 웅변가로 이름을 얻었다. 재무장관으로 1909년 「인민 예산」과 국민보험법을 내 복지국가의 토대를 놓았다. 군수장관과 육군장관을 거쳐 1916년 12월 총리가 되었다. 파리 강화회의에서는 독일 경제를 무너뜨릴 막대한 배상에 반대하고 프랑스의 패권을 견제했다. 1921년 영국-소련 무역협정을 맺고 아일랜드 자유국 수립을 협상했으나 1922년 보수당이 연립에서 빠지자 사임했다. 1936년 히틀러를 만나 찬양하기도 했다. 1945년 죽었다.
bio.en: Born in Manchester to Welsh parents, he made his name as a radical Liberal orator. As chancellor of the exchequer he introduced the 1909 People’s Budget and the National Insurance Act, laying foundations of the welfare state. After serving as minister of munitions and secretary for war he became prime minister in December 1916. At the Paris Peace Conference he opposed reparations that would wreck the German economy and sought to check French dominance. In 1921 he concluded the Anglo-Soviet Trade Agreement and negotiated the creation of the Irish Free State, but resigned in 1922 when the Conservatives left the coalition. In 1936 he met Hitler and praised him. He died in 1945.

evidence.excerpt: David Lloyd George, 1st Earl Lloyd-George of Dwyfor (17 January 1863 – 26 March 1945)

evidence.claim: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom 1916–1922
evidence.excerpt: was Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1916 to 1922
to Welsh parents William George and Elizabeth Lloyd George
He was raised with Welsh as his first language

Lloyd George gained a reputation as an orator and proponent of a Welsh blend of radical Liberal ideas that included support for Welsh devolution, the disestablishment of the Church of England in Wales, equality for labourers and tenant farmers, and reform of land ownership.
he proposed taxes on land ownership and high incomes in the 1909 People's Budget, which the Conservative-dominated House of Lords rejected
His budget was enacted in 1910, with the National Insurance Act 1911 and other measures helping to establish the modern welfare state.
In 1915, Lloyd George became Minister of Munitions and expanded artillery shell production for the war. In 1916, he was appointed Secretary of State for War
Asquith proved ineffective as prime minister and was replaced by Lloyd George in December 1916.  He centralised authority by creating a smaller war cabinet.

evidence.claim: clashed at Paris; opposed crushing reparations
evidence.excerpt: Lloyd George represented Britain at the Paris Peace Conference, clashing with French Prime Minister Georges Clemenceau, US President Woodrow Wilson, and Italian Prime Minister Vittorio Orlando.

evidence.claim: did not want to destroy the German economy
evidence.excerpt: He did not want to utterly destroy the German economy and political system—as Clemenceau demanded—with massive reparations.
Instead of handing over Upper Silesia (2,073,000 people), and the southern part of East Prussia (720,000 people) to Poland as was planned before, the plebiscite was organised.
In 1921, Lloyd George successfully concluded the Anglo-Soviet Trade Agreement.
which lasted until Lloyd George negotiated independence for the Irish Free State in 1921
The Carlton Club meeting decided the Conservatives should end the coalition and contest the next election alone. Lloyd George resigned as prime minister
Lloyd George was consistently pro-German after 1923, in part due to his growing conviction that Germany had been treated unfairly at Versailles.
In September 1936, he visited Germany to talk with Hitler. Hitler said he was pleased to have met "the man who won the war"; Lloyd George was moved, and called Hitler "the greatest living German".
Lloyd George died of cancer at the age of 82 on 26 March 1945

evidence.claim: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom

After H. H. Asquith succeeded to the premiership in 1908, Lloyd George replaced him as Chancellor of the Exchequer.

British representative at the Paris Peace Conference

epithet.ko: 카포레토 뒤 총리로 승전을 이끌었으나 강화회의에서 영토 요구를 이루지 못한 정치가
epithet.en: Italian prime minister who led the country to victory after Caporetto but failed to win its territorial claims at the peace conference

bio.ko: 팔레르모에서 태어나 이름난 법학 교수가 되었고, 1897년부터 하원의원으로 활동한 자유주의자였다. 1917년 10월 카포레토 패전으로 정부가 무너지자 총리가 되어 카도르나를 해임하고 군을 재정비했으며, 1918년 비토리오 베네토 승리로 「승리의 총리」라 불렸다. 강화회의에서 런던 조약이 약속한 달마티아와 피우메를 요구했으나 얻지 못해 1919년 4월 회의를 떠났고 6월 사임했다. 「불구의 승리」는 무솔리니가 일어선 배경이 되었다. 처음엔 무솔리니를 지지했으나 1924년 마테오티 살해 뒤 결별했다. 1952년 로마에서 죽었다.
bio.en: Born in Palermo, he became a renowned law professor and from 1897 sat in the Chamber of Deputies as a Liberal. When the government fell after the defeat at Caporetto in October 1917 he became prime minister, dismissed Cadorna and rebuilt the army, and the victory of Vittorio Veneto in 1918 earned him the name “Premier of Victory”. At the peace conference he demanded Dalmatia, promised by the Treaty of London, and Fiume, obtained neither, walked out in April 1919 and resigned in June. The “mutilated victory” helped Mussolini’s rise. He at first supported Mussolini but broke with him after the murder of Matteotti in 1924. He died in Rome in 1952.

evidence.excerpt: 19 May 1860 – 1 December 1952
was an Italian statesman, who served as the prime minister of Italy from October 1917 to June 1919
Orlando was born in Palermo, Sicily.

evidence.claim: law professor; deputy from 1897; aligned with Giolitti
evidence.excerpt: Orlando taught law at the University of Palermo and was recognized as an eminent jurist. In 1897, he was elected in the Italian Chamber of Deputies
He aligned himself with Giovanni Giolitti
After the Italian military disaster in World War I at Caporetto on 25 October 1917, which led to the fall of the Boselli government, Orlando became prime minister
Orlando's first act as head of the government was to fire General Luigi Cadorna and appoint the well-respected General Armando Diaz in his place.
The fact that Italy recovered and ended up on the winning side in 1918 earned for Orlando the title "Premier of Victory."

evidence.claim: claimed Fiume and Dalmatia, received neither
evidence.excerpt: Italy ended up claiming both and received neither, running up against Wilson's policy of national self-determination.
Italy was promised significant territorial gains in Dalmatia.
Orlando dramatically left the conference early on April 24, 1919.

Orlando resigned on 23 June 1919, following his inability to acquire Fiume for Italy in the peace settlement. The so-called "Mutilated victory" was one of the causes of the rising of Benito Mussolini.

evidence.claim: supported then broke with Mussolini over Matteotti
evidence.excerpt: When Benito Mussolini seized power in 1922, Orlando initially tactically supported him, but broke with him over the murder of Giacomo Matteotti in 1924.
Other authors say that Orlando was connected to the Mafia and mafiosi from beginning to end of his long parliamentary career, but no court ever investigated the issue.
In 1946, he was elected to the Constituent Assembly of Italy.
He died in 1952 in Rome.
served as the prime minister of Italy from October 1917 to June 1919

epithet.ko: 생제르맹 조약에 서명하고 1945년 제2공화국을 세운 오스트리아 사회민주당 지도자
epithet.en: Austrian Social Democratic leader who signed the Treaty of Saint-Germain and founded the Second Republic in 1945

bio.ko: 모라비아의 독일계 농가에서 태어나 빈에서 법학을 공부했고, 사회민주당에 들어가 1907년 제국의회 의원이 되었다. 민족 문제에서 「개인적 자치」를 내세운 오스트리아 마르크스주의 이론가로, 레닌과 스탈린의 비판을 받았다. 1918년 독일-오스트리아 공화국의 첫 총리가 되어 대연정을 이끌며 8시간 노동제 등을 도입했고, 생제르맹 조약으로 독일과의 합병 금지와 영토 상실을 받아들여야 했다. 1938년 합병을 지지했다. 1945년 4월 소련군의 지시로 임시정부를 세웠고 그해 대통령이 되었다. 1950년 빈에서 죽었다.
bio.en: Born to an ethnic German farming family in Moravia, he studied law in Vienna, joined the Social Democrats and entered the Imperial Council in 1907. An Austromarxist theorist of “personal autonomy” on the national question, he was criticised by Lenin and Stalin. In 1918 he became the first chancellor of German-Austria, leading a grand coalition that introduced the eight-hour day among other reforms, and had to accept the ban on union with Germany and the territorial losses of Saint-Germain. He supported the Anschluss in 1938. In April 1945, at Soviet direction, he formed a provisional government, and that year became president. He died in Vienna in 1950.

evidence.excerpt: Karl Renner (14 December 1870 – 31 December 1950)
was an Austrian politician and jurist of the Social Democratic Workers' Party of Austria
Renner was born the 18th child of an ethnic German family of poor wine-growers in Unter-Tannowitz
From 1890 to 1896 he studied law at the University of Vienna.

In 1896, he joined the Social Democratic Workers' Party of Austria (SDAP), representing the party in the National Council (German: Reichsrat) from the 1907 elections until its dissolution in November 1918.
he founded and edited the party's journal, Der Kampf, together with Otto Bauer and Adolf Braun
On the nationality question, he upheld the so-called "personal autonomy"
As a theorist he was reckoned as one of the leaders of Austro-Marxism.

evidence.excerpt: His and Otto Bauer's ideas about the legal protection of cultural minorities were taken up by the Jewish Bund, but fiercely denounced by Vladimir Lenin. Joseph Stalin devoted a whole chapter to criticising Cultural National Autonomy in Marxism and the National Question.
Renner became the first head of government ("State Chancellor") of that newly established small German-speaking republic

backed by a grand coalition of Social Democrats and Christian Social Party. A wide range of social reforms were introduced by Renner's government, including unemployment insurance, paid holidays, the eight-hour workday
He was the leader of the delegation that represented this new German-Austria in the negotiations of St. Germain

evidence.claim: accepted ban on union and territorial losses
evidence.excerpt: There Renner had to accept that this new Austria was prohibited any political association with Germany and he had to accept the loss of German-speaking South Tyrol and the German-speaking parts of Bohemia and Moravia where he himself was born
he even welcomed the Anschluss in 1938

evidence.claim: Soviets instructed him to form a provisional government
evidence.excerpt: On 20 April 1945, the Soviets, without asking their Western allies, instructed Renner to form a provisional government. Seven days later Renner's cabinet took office, declared the independence of Austria from Nazi Germany

epithet.ko: 1923년 총리로 소극적 저항을 끝내고 외무장관으로 로카르노 조약을 맺은 정치가
epithet.en: Weimar chancellor who ended passive resistance in 1923 and, as foreign minister, concluded the Locarno treaties

bio.ko: 베를린에서 태어나 1907년 국민자유당 의원이 되었고, 1차 세계대전 중에는 영토 병합과 무제한 잠수함전을 주장했다. 패전 뒤 독일인민당을 세웠고 점차 공화국을 받아들였다. 1923년 8월 총리 겸 외무장관이 되어 루르의 소극적 저항을 끝내고, 공산당이 들어간 작센·튀링겐 정부를 군대로 몰아냈으며, 렌텐마르크로 초인플레이션을 잡았다. 11월 불신임으로 물러났지만 죽을 때까지 외무장관으로 남아 도스안과 로카르노 조약, 국제연맹 가입을 이끌었고 1926년 노벨 평화상을 받았다. 1929년 뇌졸중으로 죽었다.
bio.en: Born in Berlin, he entered the Reichstag for the National Liberals in 1907 and during the war backed annexations and unrestricted submarine warfare. After the defeat he founded the German People’s Party and came to accept the republic. Chancellor and foreign minister from August 1923, he ended passive resistance in the Ruhr, used the army to remove the Saxon and Thuringian governments that included Communists, and halted hyperinflation with the Rentenmark. Ousted by a no-confidence vote in November, he remained foreign minister until his death, shaping the Dawes Plan, the Locarno treaties and entry into the League of Nations, and shared the 1926 Nobel Peace Prize. He died of a stroke in 1929.

evidence.excerpt: 10 May 1878 – 3 October 1929

evidence.claim: German statesman of the Weimar Republic
evidence.excerpt: was a German statesman during the Weimar Republic who served as chancellor of Germany from August to November 1923 and as foreign minister from 1923 to 1929

His father worked as a beer bottler and distributor

evidence.claim: studied political economy at Berlin and Leipzig
evidence.excerpt: Stresemann attended the University of Berlin and Leipzig University, where he studied political economy, history and international law
In 1907, he was elected to the Reichstag as a deputy for the National Liberal Party.
During World War I, he was a vocal advocate for German militarism and expansionism.
He believed that Germany would need to annex Belgium, parts of north-east France, "extensive" lands in Eastern Europe and the French protectorate in Morocco
He was a vocal proponent of unrestricted submarine warfare.
He founded the German People's Party (DVP) and, despite his own monarchist beliefs, came to grudgingly accept Weimar democracy
Initially, Stresemann and the DVP opposed the Weimar Republic and supported a restoration of the monarchy.
Stresemann was regarded as a Vernunftrepublikaner, (republican by reason)
On 13 August 1923, Stresemann was appointed chancellor and foreign minister of a grand coalition government
On 26 September 1923, Stresemann announced the end to the passive resistance against the occupation of the Ruhr by the French and Belgians
Stresemann used a Reichsexekution to send troops into the two states to remove the Communists from the governments
The Stresemann government introduced a new currency, the Rentenmark, to end hyperinflation.
after he lost a confidence vote on 23 November 1923, Stresemann and his cabinet resigned
Stresemann remained as foreign minister in the government of his successor, Wilhelm Marx from the Centre Party, and for the rest of his life

led to Germany's admission to the League of Nations a year later. Stresemann also moved to improve relations with the Soviet Union through the 1926 Treaty of Berlin.
Stresemann was co-winner with Aristide Briand of the 1926 Nobel Peace Prize for their work on Locarno.

epithet.ko: 갈리폴리에서 이름을 얻고 국민운동을 이끌어 튀르키예 공화국을 세운 대통령
epithet.en: Gallipoli commander who led the national movement and founded the Republic of Turkey as its first president

bio.ko: 살로니카에서 태어나 청년 튀르크 운동에 가담했고, 1차 세계대전 때 갈리폴리 방어로 이름을 얻었다. 패전 뒤 1919년 5월 삼순에 상륙해 점령에 맞선 국민운동을 조직했고, 1920년 앙카라에 대국민의회를 열었다. 볼셰비키 정부의 금과 무기 지원을 받아 그리스군을 물리쳤고, 로잔 조약으로 승리를 인정받았다. 이 시기 아나톨리아의 아르메니아인·그리스인에 대한 인종 청소가 학살·추방·주민 교환으로 마무리되었다. 1922년 술탄제를 폐지하고 1923년 공화국의 초대 대통령이 되어 일당 체제 아래 세속화와 튀르크화 정책을 폈다. 1938년 죽었다.
bio.en: Born in Salonica, he joined the Young Turk movement and made his name defending Gallipoli in the First World War. After the defeat he landed at Samsun in May 1919 to organise the national movement against occupation, and in 1920 convened the Grand National Assembly in Ankara. With gold and arms from the Bolshevik government he defeated the Greek army, and the Treaty of Lausanne recognised the victory. In these years the ethnic cleansing of Anatolia’s Armenians and Greeks was completed through massacres, deportations and population exchange. He abolished the sultanate in 1922 and in 1923 became the first president of the republic, pursuing secularising reforms and Turkification under one-party rule. He died in 1938.

evidence.excerpt: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk (c. 1881 – 10 November 1938) was a Turkish field marshal and statesman

evidence.claim: Founder and first president of the Republic of Turkey
evidence.excerpt: was the founder of the Republic of Turkey and served as its first president from 1923 until his death in 1938
was a Turkish field marshal and statesman

evidence.claim: born in Salonica; CUP and Young Turks
evidence.excerpt: Born in Salonica in the Ottoman Empire, Atatürk was early on persecuted for agitating against Sultan Abdul Hamid II's autocracy, joining opposition movements like the Committee of Union and Progress and the Young Turks.

evidence.claim: sidelined after denouncing the CUP leadership
evidence.excerpt: Atatürk denounced CUP leadership for encouraging a politicised military –and was subsequently sidelined–
He rose to prominence with his role in the Defence of Gallipoli during World War I.
Mustafa Kemal was given the task of organizing and commanding the 19th Division attached to the Fifth Army during the Battle of Gallipoli.

evidence.claim: reached Samsun, organised a national movement
evidence.excerpt: On 19 May 1919, he reached Samsun. His first goal was the establishment of an organized national movement against the occupying forces.

evidence.claim: GNA opened in April 1920 with him as speaker
evidence.excerpt: On 23 April 1920, the GNA opened with Mustafa Kemal as the speaker

evidence.claim: Greek forces advancing from Smyrna, occupied May 1919

epithet.ko: 힌덴부르크와 함께 독일의 전쟁을 지휘하고 전후 맥주홀 폭동에 가담한 장군
epithet.en: General who directed Germany’s war with Hindenburg and later joined Hitler’s Beer Hall Putsch

bio.ko: 포젠주의 평민 집안에서 태어나 참모본부에서 일했고, 1914년 리에주와 탄넨베르크로 이름을 얻었다. 1916년 8월 힌덴부르크와 함께 최고사령부를 넘겨받아 제1병참총감으로서 사실상의 군사독재 아래 전쟁을 지휘하고 힌덴부르크 계획을 밀어붙였다. 1918년 3월 미하엘 작전으로 춘계 공세를 열었으나 실패했고, 9월 즉각 휴전을 요구한 뒤 10월 해임되었다. 전후 비수설을 퍼뜨렸고 1920년 카프 폭동과 1923년 히틀러의 맥주홀 폭동에 가담했다. 1924~1928년 국가사회주의 자유운동 의원을 지냈다. 1937년 뮌헨에서 죽었다.
bio.en: Born to a commoner family in the Province of Posen, he served on the General Staff and won fame at Liège and Tannenberg in 1914. In August 1916 he and Hindenburg took over the Supreme Army Command; as First Quartermaster General he directed the war under a de facto military dictatorship and drove the Hindenburg Programme. His spring offensive, opened with Operation Michael in March 1918, failed; in September he demanded an immediate armistice and in October he was dismissed. After the war he spread the stab-in-the-back myth and took part in the Kapp Putsch of 1920 and Hitler’s Beer Hall Putsch of 1923. He sat in the Reichstag for the National Socialist Freedom Movement in 1924–1928 and died in Munich in 1937.

After the war, Ludendorff became a prominent nationalist leader and a promoter of the stab-in-the-back myth, which posited that Germany's defeat and the settlement reached at Versailles were the result of a treasonous conspiracy by Marxists, Freemasons and Jews.

epithet.ko: 7월 위기에 오스트리아를 지원하고 1918년 퇴위해 망명한 마지막 독일 황제
epithet.en: Last German Emperor, who backed Austria-Hungary in the July Crisis and abdicated and fled in 1918

bio.ko: 프로이센 왕세자와 영국 빅토리아 여왕의 맏딸 사이에서 태어나 1888년 황제가 되었고, 1890년 비스마르크를 해임했다. 1900년 의화단 진압군에게 훈족처럼 싸우라고 연설했고, 함대 증강과 모로코 개입으로 독일을 고립시켰다. 1914년 7월 위기 때 오스트리아-헝가리에 군사 지원을 보장했다. 전쟁 중에는 결정을 최고사령부에 넘겨 힌덴부르크와 루덴도르프의 군사독재가 섰다. 1918년 11월 9일 퇴위가 발표되자 네덜란드로 망명했고, 네덜란드는 베르사유 조약이 정한 그의 인도를 거부했다. 1941년 도른에서 죽었다.
bio.en: The son of the Prussian crown prince and Queen Victoria’s eldest daughter, he became emperor in 1888 and dismissed Bismarck in 1890. In 1900 he urged the troops sent against the Boxers to fight like Huns, and his naval build-up and Moroccan interventions isolated Germany. In the July Crisis of 1914 he assured Austria-Hungary of military support. In the war he left decisions largely to the Supreme Army Command, leading to the de facto military dictatorship of Hindenburg and Ludendorff. When his abdication was announced on 9 November 1918 he went into exile in the Netherlands, which refused to extradite him as the Treaty of Versailles provided. He died at Doorn in 1941.

epithet.ko: 1918년 연합군 총사령관으로 반격을 이끌고 휴전 조건을 받아 낸 프랑스 원수
epithet.en: French marshal who as Allied supreme commander in 1918 led the counter-offensive and dictated the armistice

bio.ko: 타르브의 가톨릭 집안에서 태어났다. 1914년 마른 전투에서 제9군을 지휘해 이름을 얻었다. 1918년 3월 독일의 춘계 공세 앞에서 연합군 총사령관이 되어 프랑스·영국·미국군을 조율했고, 제2차 마른 전투 뒤 원수가 되어 전쟁을 끝낸 반격을 이끌었다. 11월 콩피에뉴에서 독일의 휴전 서명을 받았다. 강화회의에서 라인란트 분리를 주장했으나 15년 점령에 그치자 베르사유 조약이 너무 관대하다고 비판했다. 1920년 폴란드-소비에트 전쟁에서 폴란드에 조언해 폴란드 원수 칭호를 받았다. 1929년 파리에서 죽었다.
bio.en: Born into a Catholic family in Tarbes, he made his name commanding the Ninth Army at the Marne in 1914. Facing the German spring offensive in March 1918 he became Allied supreme commander, coordinating the French, British and American armies, and after the Second Battle of the Marne was made marshal and led the counter-offensive that ended the war. In November he received the German armistice at Compiègne. At the peace conference he called for separating the Rhineland, and when this was reduced to a fifteen-year occupation he criticised the Treaty of Versailles as too lenient. For his advice to Poland in the Polish-Soviet War of 1920 he was made a Marshal of Poland. He died in Paris in 1929.

epithet.ko: 「세 파샤」의 전쟁장관으로 오스만을 참전시키고 아르메니아인 제노사이드를 주도한 군인
epithet.en: War minister among the Three Pashas who took the Ottomans into the war and was a main perpetrator of the Armenian genocide

bio.ko: 콘스탄티노플에서 태어나 통일진보위원회에 들어갔고 1908년 청년 튀르크 혁명의 영웅이 되었다. 1913년 쿠데타로 정부를 무너뜨리고 전쟁장관이 되어 탈라트·제말과 「세 파샤」로 제국을 다스렸다. 독일과의 동맹으로 오스만을 1차 세계대전에 끌어들였고, 1914년 12월 사르카미시에서 대군을 잃은 뒤 패배를 아르메니아인 탓으로 돌렸다. 아르메니아인·그리스인·아시리아인 제노사이드의 주요 가해자였다. 패전 뒤 달아나 궐석 사형을 선고받았다. 볼셰비키와 손잡았다가 1921년 중앙아시아에서 바스마치 반란군 편으로 넘어갔고, 1922년 붉은군대와 싸우다 죽었다.
bio.en: Born in Constantinople, he joined the Committee of Union and Progress and became a hero of the Young Turk Revolution of 1908. After the 1913 coup he became war minister and ruled the empire with Talat and Djemal as the Three Pashas. He took the Ottomans into the First World War in alliance with Germany, and after losing most of his army at Sarıkamış in December 1914 blamed the defeat on the Armenians. He was a main perpetrator of the Armenian, Greek and Assyrian genocides. After the defeat he fled and was sentenced to death in absentia. He worked with the Bolsheviks, then in 1921 in Central Asia went over to the Basmachi rebels, and was killed fighting the Red Army in 1922.
